content.text: The cause is on line 12 of `solution/core.py`. When an interval is contained in the previous one, the code sets the merged end to `b` instead of `max(pb, b)`, so `(1,4)` absorbing `(2,3)` shrinks to `(1,3)`. The same line handles `(1,3)` absorbing `(2,2)`, which gives `(1,2)`. I'll make that one change.

content.text: The visible suite now passes (2 passed). I changed one line in `solution/core.py`: the merge step at line 12 now sets the merged end to `max(pb, b)` instead of `b`. The cause was that a contained interval overwrote the end of the interval that contained it, so `(1, 4)` followed by `(2, 3)` shrank to `(1, 3)`, and `(1, 3)` followed by `(2, 2)` shrank to `(1, 2)`. I left the touching logic and the public `merge` signature alone. Spot checks also give `[(1, 2), (2, 3)]` for touching intervals with `join_touching=False` and `[(1, 3)]` with the default, which look right. I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
